neighbours.label: ' said' (or ' knew', ' told') right after a subject, introducing indirect reported speech without quotation marks
fire: The mayor said that the new bridge would open to traffic before the end of the summer.
Police said three people had been taken to hospital after the crash on the motorway.
The company said its profits had fallen sharply because of the cold weather.
A spokesman for the ministry said the talks would continue next week in Geneva.
Her doctor said she could go back to work as soon as the cast was removed.
Witnesses said the fire started in the kitchen shortly after midnight.
The coach said the team had played its best football of the season on Saturday.
Researchers said the drug could be available to patients within five years.
quiet: The mayor's new bridge will open to traffic before the end of the summer, according to the plans.
Three people were taken to hospital after the crash on the motorway on Tuesday night.
The company's profits fell sharply this quarter because of the cold weather in the north.
Talks between the ministry and the unions will continue next week in Geneva.
She went back to work as soon as the cast on her arm was finally removed.
The fire started in the kitchen shortly after midnight and spread to the roof.
The team played its best football of the season on Saturday in front of a full stadium.
The new drug could be available to patients within five years if trials go well.

notes: Card: top 32 peak on ' said' x24, ' knew', ' told' before a that-clause; the - pole is the opening quotation mark of direct speech, so the pole pair looks like indirect vs direct speech. Output promotes past-tense ' was', ' were', ' had'.
